# Data and lineage

```{r}
#| include: false
source(here::here("chapters", "_setup.R"))
```

## Source

The data are one file, `licorice_gargle.csv`, emailed by the PI's fellow.
It is the public version of the trial data from the `medicaldata` R
package, with one row per patient. The codebook is
`notes/2026-10-16-codebook.md`. The file's date of receipt and its MD5
checksum are in `data/README.md`. The raw file is never edited, and
`scripts/02_make_analysis_data.R` refuses to run if its bytes change
(D-019).

Cleaning (`clean_raw()`) checks every column against the codebook. An
unexpected code, an out-of-range or fractional score, or text in a numeric
column stops the pipeline and names the rows. The delivered file passed
every check. The file has no patient identifier, so each patient's
identifier is their row number in the raw file.

```{r}
#| eval: !expr '!has_data'
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
cat("*No data yet. Run `make results` once the raw file is in `data/raw/`.*\n")
```

## Lineage

Each step is a function in `R/` with tests in `tests/testthat/`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_data
knitr::kable(lineage, col.names = c("Step", "Rows", "File"))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_data
n_arm <- results$n_by_arm
miss <- results$missing
n_absent <- results$n_enrolled - results$n_patients
# Each data-dependent sentence is built here, with a branch for each way
# the data could fall, so the prose cannot outlive the numbers.
s_patients <- sprintf(
  "The file has %d patients: %d randomized to sugar water and %d to licorice.",
  results$n_patients, n_arm[["Sugar water"]], n_arm[["Licorice"]]
)
s_enrolled <- if (n_absent > 0) {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "The codebook gives an enrollment count of %d, so %d enrolled %s not in the file.",
      "Why is an open question for the client (Chapter 1). If a randomized patient",
      "is missing, the analysis is not fully intention to treat."
    ),
    results$n_enrolled, n_absent, if (n_absent == 1) "patient is" else "patients are"
  )
} else {
  sprintf("The file holds every one of the %d patients the codebook counts as enrolled.",
          results$n_enrolled)
}
missing_by_patient <- miss$missing_sugar + miss$missing_licorice
s_missing <- if (all(missing_by_patient == results$no_postop_n)) {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "Missing outcomes come entirely from %d patients (%d on sugar water, %d on",
      "licorice) who have no post-operative data at all; every other patient has all",
      "four scores."
    ),
    results$no_postop_n, miss$missing_sugar[1], miss$missing_licorice[1]
  )
} else {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "%d patients have no post-operative data at all; other patients are missing",
      "some assessments but not others (see the table)."
    ),
    results$no_postop_n
  )
}
s_trigger <- if (max(miss$prop_missing) <= 0.05) {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "At most %s of patients are missing any one assessment. That is within the",
      "plan's five-percent trigger for revisiting the missing-data approach (D-015),",
      "so the complete-case analyses stand."
    ),
    fmt_pct(max(miss$prop_missing), 1)
  )
} else {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "Up to %s of patients are missing an assessment, above the plan's five-percent",
      "trigger: the missing-data approach must be revisited before these results are",
      "used (D-015)."
    ),
    fmt_pct(max(miss$prop_missing), 1)
  )
}
b <- results$bounds
ab <- results$absent_bound
s_bounds <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "Among the patients in the file, the best case for licorice gives %s and the",
    "worst case %s. The complete-case estimate (Chapter 6) is %s."
  ),
  fmt_or(b[1, ]), fmt_or(b[2, ]), fmt_or(results$primary)
)
s_bounds_verdict <- if (all(b$upper < 1)) {
  paste(
    "Both bounds keep the confidence interval below one, so the missing outcomes of",
    "patients in the file cannot change the primary conclusion."
  )
} else {
  paste(
    "At least one bound has a confidence interval that includes one, so the missing",
    "outcomes of patients in the file could change the primary conclusion."
  )
}
s_absent <- if (ab$n_absent > 0) {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "These bounds do not cover the %d enrolled %s absent from the file. *Added after",
      "results were seen (post hoc; D-021):* adding %s to the licorice arm with a sore",
      "throat, on top of the in-file worst case, gives %s. %s"
    ),
    ab$n_absent, if (ab$n_absent == 1) "patient" else "patients",
    if (ab$n_absent == 1) "that patient" else "those patients",
    fmt_or(ab),
    if (ab$upper < 1) {
      "The confidence interval stays below one, so the primary conclusion holds even then."
    } else {
      "The confidence interval then includes one, so the absent patients could matter."
    }
  )
} else {
  "No enrolled patient is absent from the file, so the bounds cover every enrolled patient."
}
```

`r if (has_data) s_patients else ""`
`r if (has_data) s_enrolled else ""`

## Missing data

Any missing score is treated as missing, and each analysis uses the
patients observed at that assessment (complete case; D-010, D-015).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_data
#| tbl-cap: "Patients missing the sore-throat score at each assessment, by arm."
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Assessment = miss$assessment,
    `Sugar water` = sprintf("%d of %d", miss$missing_sugar, miss$n_sugar),
    Licorice = sprintf("%d of %d", miss$missing_licorice, miss$n_licorice),
    `Missing overall` = fmt_pct(miss$prop_missing, 1),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
)
```

`r if (has_data) s_missing else ""`
The intake notes anticipated patients with no post-operative data ("a
couple pts no post-op data"). Why they have none is an open question in
Chapter 1.
`r if (has_data) s_trigger else ""`

### Best- and worst-case bounds for the primary outcome

The plan bounds the primary odds ratio by filling in every missing primary
outcome among the patients in the file, in the way most and least
favourable to licorice (Chapter 3).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_data
#| tbl-cap: "Primary odds ratio (licorice against sugar water) with missing outcomes filled in."
all_bounds <- rbind(cbind(b, n_absent = 0), ab)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Bound = c(b$bound, paste(ab$bound, "(post hoc)")),
    `Outcomes filled in` = all_bounds$n_filled,
    `Absent patients added` = all_bounds$n_absent,
    `Odds ratio (95% CI)` = fmt_or_cell(all_bounds$or, all_bounds$lower, all_bounds$upper),
    `p-value` = fmt_p(all_bounds$p_value),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
)
```

`r if (has_data) s_bounds else ""`
`r if (has_data) s_bounds_verdict else ""`

`r if (has_data) s_absent else ""`
